prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but to recommend a specific reliable contractor I need either permission to look up current local listings (I don’t have live browsing in this chat) or some more details from you. If you want a quick, safe path right now, here’s a practical plan plus a vetting checklist so you can find a trustworthy Joplin contractor and compare options.

Quick questions
- What kind of work? (bathroom/kitchen remodel, roof, foundation, HVAC, plumbing/electrical, general whole‑house remodel, small repairs)
- Rough budget and timeline?
- Is the property owner‑occupied or a rental/investment?
- Do you need a contractor who handles permits/inspections and subtrades, or just a trade specialist?

Where to find reliable local contractors
- Google Maps / Google Reviews (search “home remodel contractor Joplin, MO”)
- Angi, HomeAdvisor, Houzz (for local pros and project photos)
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) — look for A ratings and complaint history
- Joplin Area Chamber of Commerce directory
- Local Facebook neighborhood groups, Nextdoor — for recent homeowner referrals
- Missouri Division of Professional Registration (for licensed trades where applicable)
- Word‑of‑mouth: ask neighbors, realtors, or local building suppliers for who they trust

Vetting checklist (use this when you call or meet)
1. License & insurance
   - Ask for contractor license number (if required for the work) and verify.
   - Ask for proof of general liability insurance and workers’ compensation.
2. References & portfolio
   - Request 3 recent references and photos of completed projects similar to yours.
   - Drive by (if public) to see work in person.
3. Written estimate & scope
   - Get at least 3 written bids with itemized scopes, materials, and brands.
   - Compare apples to apples — same materials, same scope.
4. Contract & payments
   - Use a written contract with scope, schedule, payment schedule, start/end dates, change order process, warranty, and cleanup details.
   - Typical down payment: modest (often 10–30%), then progress payments tied to milestones.
   - Never pay full amount up front.
5. Permits & inspections
   - Confirm who obtains permits and handles inspections; complex work should include permits.
6. Timeline & subcontractors
   - Ask who will be on site (owner, project manager, subs) and get a communication plan.
7. Lien waivers & warranties
   - Request lien waivers on payments and written warranties for labor and materials.
8. Red flags
   - Large up‑front cash demand, only a P.O. box, no local phone number, no written contract, bad or no references.

Interview questions to ask a contractor
- How many similar projects have you completed in Joplin?
- Can you provide local references and a recent project portfolio?
- Who will manage the job day‑to‑day?
- What is the projected start date and completion timeline?
- How do you handle unexpected problems or change orders?
- Who obtains permits and schedules inspections?
- What warranties do you provide?

If you want, I can:
- Draft an email or phone script you can use to contact contractors.
- Provide a sample checklist/contract items to include.
- Help evaluate estimates if you paste them here.
- If you want specific names, tell me you want me to search and I’ll explain how to do that or you can paste candidate names and I’ll help evaluate them.

Which of the above would you like next?
